item.title: Over 2,000 climbers make trek up formerly-known Hancock Tower in downtown Chicago for lung health awareness
item.description: In Sunday morning's annual Hustle Chicago stair climb, formerly known as the Hancock Hustle, more than 2,000 people climbed 1,632 steps over 94 floors to the top of the skyscraper at 875 North Michigan Avenue to help raise funds and awareness for lung health.

item.title: Twin Milan and Cortina Olympic cauldrons are extinguished, signaling the end of Winter Games
item.description: VERONA, Italy (AP) — The Milan Cortina Olympics ended Sunday as the twin flames in co-host cities Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo were extinguished during a closing ceremony inside the ancient Verona Arena, roughly mid-distance between the far-flung mountain, valley and city venues that made these the most spread-out Winter Games ever. item.title: 12th annual pancake breakfast raises money for Get Behind The Vest Program
item.description: The 12th annual Get Behind the Vest Pancake Breakfast has raised over $850,000 to help replace bulletproof vests for Chicago police officers, with all donations going to the Chicago Police Memorial Foundation.

item.title: Jack Hughes' OT goal delivers Olympic gold medal for U.S. men's hockey team in thrilling 2-1 win over Canada
item.description: For the first time since the legendary 1980 "Miracle on Ice" squad, the U.S. men's hockey team has won the Olympic gold medal, as Jack Hughes scored 1:41 into overtime and the U.S. defeated Canada, 2-1, in a thrilling gold medal final Sunday morning on the final day of the Milan Cortina Olympics.

item.title: Parents push back on Archdiocese of Chicago’s decision to close six schools
item.description: Parents from St. Hubert Catholic School and other affected schools are protesting the Chicago Archdiocese's decision to close six schools, citing a lack of communication and clarity regarding the school's financial standing.

item.title: Behind the scenes of CPD's Community Training Observation Day
item.description: The Chicago Police Department has launched its first-ever Community Training Observation Day (CTOD) to build public trust, which includes taking members of the public through a version of the training every officer is required to take.

item.title: Monday Forecast: Bitter wind chills, flurries across Chicagoland
item.description: Monday's high temperatures will only reach the upper 20s, and single-digit wind chills will make it feel much colder throughout the day. A mix of sun and clouds is expected, with the chance for a few more flurries late in the evening.

item.title: TSA says PreCheck still operational after previous announcement of suspension during funding fight
item.description: The Transportation Security Administration said Sunday that its PreCheck program would remain operational despite an earlier announcement from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security that the airport security service was being suspended during the partial government shutdown.

item.title: Postal workers rally for fair wages, safer conditions ahead of contract negotiations
item.description: Postal workers across the country rallied for fair contracts and safer working conditions ahead of negotiations set to begin this week in Washington, D.C.
